ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in Central America and the Caribbean changed by +0.038 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.013 to +0.064), which is statistically significant (p = 0.0026). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.095 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in Central America and the Caribbean changed by +0.11 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.01 to +0.22), which is statistically significant (p = 0.04). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.27 mm/day.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in Central America and the Caribbean shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.59): the estimate is −0.04 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.21 to +0.11). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
